origins.section: 10.1. Certification Proves One Host Link Against One Network's Specification
10.3. A Case Is a Request Template and Every Field Its Answer Must Carry
10.4. A Test Card Is Issued for Testing, and the Luhn Check Only Says It Is Well Formed
10.5. The Evidence Is the Bytes That Left, Kept as Text and Found by STAN
10.6. The Certified Build Is the One That Goes Live

gates.says: all 5 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-second-network: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-second-network: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-second-network: 10.1 says none of the kernel approval, the PCI DSS assessment or a host certification with the first network covers the new link, and the network switches on live traffic only after its own script has passed on its own test host.
recorded.prompt:q-replayed-session: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-replayed-session: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-replayed-session: 10.3 says a replayed recorded message repeats the STAN and field 7 the host already saw, and a host that checks for duplicates answers 94, duplicate transmission.
recorded.prompt:q-generated-numbers: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-generated-numbers: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-generated-numbers: 10.4 says the check digit says nothing about who the card belongs to (real cards pass it too), and a number generated under a network's prefix with a correct check digit may be a real cardholder's.
recorded.prompt:q-terminal-id-dispute: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-terminal-id-dispute: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-terminal-id-dispute: 10.5 says the log shows the message as the program built it, the packager padded the short value on the way out, and the evidence is the hex dump of the bytes that left, kept as text and found by STAN.
recorded.prompt:q-library-upgrade: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-library-upgrade: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-library-upgrade: 10.6 says the network certified bytes, a library or packager change can alter them, and after a library version change you should ask the network whether you must certify again.

gates.says: all 15 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-second-network:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-second-network:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-second-network:b: 10.1 says PCI programmes are assessed separately and none of them tests messages, while live traffic is switched on only after the network's own script passes.
recorded.prompt:q-second-network:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-second-network:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-second-network:c: 10.1 says even a host certification with the first network says nothing about the second, because each link has its own header, private fields and encodings.
recorded.prompt:q-second-network:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-second-network:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-second-network:d: 10.1 says the kernel approval is about the terminal and the assessment about how card data is kept, so neither covers the new link.
recorded.prompt:q-replayed-session:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-replayed-session:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-replayed-session:b: 10.3 and the 10.8 table say a duplicate is a request replayed with the STAN and time of an earlier one, not a second purchase on the same card.
recorded.prompt:q-replayed-session:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-replayed-session:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-replayed-session:c: 10.8 lists 94 as duplicate transmission caused by a replayed STAN and time, not a card decline, and the page never says a test card approves only once per session.
recorded.prompt:q-replayed-session:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-replayed-session:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-replayed-session:d: 10.3 and 10.8 say 94 means duplicate transmission from a replayed STAN and time, not a decline over funds still held by an earlier approval.
recorded.prompt:q-generated-numbers:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-generated-numbers:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-generated-numbers:b: 10.4 says such a generated number may be a real cardholder's, which contradicts the claim that it matches no printed card.
recorded.prompt:q-generated-numbers:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-generated-numbers:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-generated-numbers:c: 10.4 says the check digit says nothing about who the card belongs to and that test cards are issued for testing by the network or published by processors.
recorded.prompt:q-generated-numbers:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-generated-numbers:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-generated-numbers:d: 10.4 says a generated number may be a real cardholder's, whose every copy in a log or dump is card data under PCI DSS, whatever the simulator does with it.
recorded.prompt:q-terminal-id-dispute:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-terminal-id-dispute:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-terminal-id-dispute:b: 10.5 says the log differs from the bytes because the packager padded the value after the program built it, and its example log shows field 41 unmasked, with masking applied to field 2.
recorded.prompt:q-terminal-id-dispute:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-terminal-id-dispute:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-terminal-id-dispute:c: 10.5 and 10.7 say the log shows what the program built, not what the host received.
recorded.prompt:q-terminal-id-dispute:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-terminal-id-dispute:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-terminal-id-dispute:d: 10.5 says the packager padded the short value on the way out, so the padding was in the bytes sent, not added by the host's reader.
recorded.prompt:q-library-upgrade:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-library-upgrade:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-library-upgrade:b: Partly true: 10.6 does say to certify a specific build and to ask after a library version change, but it gives the reason as 'the network certified bytes', not the release number.
recorded.prompt:q-library-upgrade:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-library-upgrade:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-library-upgrade:c: 10.6 says the network certified bytes, and a library change can alter them even when the business logic is untouched.
recorded.prompt:q-library-upgrade:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-library-upgrade:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-library-upgrade:d: 10.6 says your own suite may not notice, because a simulator built on the same library changes with it.

gates.says: each of the 5 questions keys exactly 1 of its distinct options and every option carries the sentence its reader is shown
each of the 5 questions cites a passage the ledger still digests to the value this exercise was built from
